To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the 53‐ kDa glycoprotein antigen is the antigen recognized by monoclonal antibodies MEM‐15 and‐18, and is present in normal sera and urine of some nephropathic patients.
a soluble form of a monocyte surface antigen, MY‐4, was isolated and found to be related to the src gene product and to epidermal growth‐factor.
a soluble form of a 53‐kDalton monocyte antigen was found in urine of nephrotic patients, and that this antigen is related to growth factor receptors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the biochemical characterization of the soluble form of the MY‐4/53‐kDa/monocyte surface antigen.
the isolation and biochemical characterization of a monocyte‐specific antigen.
the characterization of a soluble antigen which is related to the 53‐Kd monocyte surface antigen, and which is expressed by a wide variety of cell types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the antigen recognized by MEM‐15 and -18 is the same as MY‐4 or -23, that the antigen is a 53‐kD glycoprotein which is expressed on the surface of monocytes and is present in normal sera and urine, that the antigen contains a 21‐amino acid sequence homologous to a region of the src protein, and that the antigen is related to the epidermal growth‐factor precursor.

the 53‐kd antigen is a glycoprotein with a molecular weight of approximately 52,500, which contains 1 mol of N‐acetylglucosamine, 1 mol of mannose, 1 mol each of galactose and sialic acid, and 1 mol of glucosamine per mol of protein.

a glycoprotein of Mr 53 000 has been isolated from normal human urine and that the N‐terminal amino acids are identical to the first 15 amino acids of the kinase‐related protein src and of the precursor of epo‐dermal growth factor.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the 53‐kd antigen is a glycoprotein of molecular weight 53 000 which is present in urine and in serum and is a potential tumor marker.

the MY‐4/53‐kDa protein is a glycoprotein which is expressed on monocyte and lymphocyte cell surfaces, is found in normal serum and urine of some patients with nephrotic syndrome, and has structural similarities to the src and epidermal growth factors.

the MY‐4 antigen is a glycoprotein which contains a 53‐kD core of 460 amino acids, of which the first 30 are identical to a portion of the src protein and the last 20 to a portion of epidermal‐growth‐factor‐precursor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a 53‐kD protein is a major component of urine in patients with nephrotic syndrome and that this protein may be the same as the MY‐4 antigen.
the 53‐ kDa antigen is a glycoprotein with a molecular weight of about 60 kDa, which is present in most normal sera in a soluble form.
a soluble form of this 53‐kD protein is present in normal human serum and in the urine of some nephritic patients.
